skill.name: azure-rbac
skill.description: Helps users select least privilege Azure RBAC roles for identities and produce Azure CLI and Bicep role assignment guidance.
skill.summary: Select least privilege Azure RBAC roles and draft assignment guidance.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: The two static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans around Azure RBAC permission names. No evidence found for prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or semantic misuse in the reviewed files.

static_findings.snippet: To assign RBAC roles to identities, you need a role that includes the `Microsoft.Authorization/roleA

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks are Markdown inline code around an Azure permission name, not executable syntax. The line is prose guidance and does not invoke a shell or Ruby runtime.
The backticks only format the Azure permission string inside a bullet item. No command execution, interpolation, or user-controlled shell input appears on this line.

content.user_title: Choose Least Privilege Azure RBAC Roles
content.value_statement: Azure role assignments can grant more access than intended. This skill helps select least privilege RBAC roles and draft CLI or Bicep assignment guidance.
actual_capabilities: Use Azure documentation tooling to find minimal built-in role definitions for requested permissions.
Recommend custom role definition generation when no built-in role matches required permissions.
Generate Azure CLI commands for assigning selected roles to identities.
Provide Bicep snippets for role assignments using Azure schema and best practices tools.
Explain prerequisite roles needed to grant Azure RBAC assignments.
limitations: Requires the named Azure tools to retrieve documentation and generate Azure-specific artifacts.
Does not verify live tenant permissions unless connected Azure tools provide that data.
Generated CLI and Bicep should be reviewed before applying in production.
Custom role recommendations depend on the permissions described by the user.

use_cases.title: Select Least Privilege Role
use_cases.description: Find an Azure built-in role that grants the requested access without unnecessary permissions.

use_cases.title: Prepare Role Assignment Automation
use_cases.description: Generate Azure CLI and Bicep guidance for assigning RBAC roles to identities.

use_cases.title: Check Granting Prerequisites
use_cases.description: Identify whether Owner, User Access Administrator, or a custom role is needed to grant access.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Reader Role
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a minimal data access role.
prompt_templates.prompt: I need an Azure role that lets a managed identity read blobs in one storage account. Recommend least privilege and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Assignment Commands
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for role selection and CLI guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the least privilege role for a service principal to read Key Vault secrets. Then draft Azure CLI assignment steps for subscription scope.

prompt_templates.title: Create Bicep Assignment
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for infrastructure as code guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: For an app identity that needs to start and stop virtual machines in one resource group, recommend a role and provide Bicep assignment guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Custom Role Need
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for custom role evaluation.
prompt_templates.prompt: No built-in role seems to match permissions for managing private endpoints without broader network control. Compare options and outline a custom role approach.

output_examples.input: What role should a managed identity use to read blobs from one storage account?
output_examples.output: Recommendation: Storage Blob Data Reader at storage account scope. Rationale: It grants blob read access without write or account management permissions.

output_examples.input: How do I assign an RBAC role with Bicep?
output: Selected role: the least privilege role that matches the requested action.
Assignment guidance: create a role assignment at the target scope and reference the principal ID.
Review note: confirm the deploying identity can create role assignments.

output_examples.input: No built-in role fits my exact permission set. What should I do?
output_examples.output: The skill can suggest a custom role approach, list required actions, and explain why broader built-in roles may be excessive.

best_practices: Scope assignments to the smallest subscription, resource group, or resource that satisfies the request.
Prefer built-in roles before creating custom roles, unless permissions clearly require a custom definition.
Review generated commands and Bicep against organizational access policies before deployment.
anti_patterns: Using Owner when User Access Administrator or a scoped data role is sufficient.
Assigning roles at subscription scope for access needed on one resource.
Creating broad custom roles without documenting required actions and data actions.

faq.question: Does this skill change my Azure tenant?
faq.answer: No. It produces guidance and generated commands through Azure tools. Review and run commands yourself.

faq.question: Can it choose between built-in and custom roles?
faq.answer: Yes. It first looks for a least privilege built-in role, then suggests custom role generation when needed.

faq.question: Does it support managed identities?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill can reason about role assignments for managed identities and other Azure principals.

faq.question: What permission is needed to grant roles?
faq.answer: The granting identity needs Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write, usually through User Access Administrator, Owner, or a custom role.

faq.question: Can it create Bicep guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft Bicep role assignment guidance using Azure schema and best practices tools.

faq.question: Is it limited to Azure RBAC?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill focuses on Azure RBAC role selection, assignment guidance, and granting prerequisites.
